title: Mata Mansa Devi Temple, Panchkula: Timings, Story & How to Reach
seo_title: Mansa Devi Temple Panchkula: Timings, Story, Navratri
seo_desc: Mata Mansa Devi Temple in Panchkula's Shivalik foothills: darshan and aarti timings, the legend of the three pindis, Navratri melas and how to reach.
label: Mansa Devi, Panchkula
blurb: Shivalik shrine of the three pindis, near Chandigarh
tag: Three stones on a Shivalik hill, and a goddess of the heart's wishes.
sub: Shri Mata Mansa Devi Mandir stands in the Shivalik foothills of Panchkula, just outside Chandigarh. Its story, darshan and aarti timings, the two Navratri melas, and the easiest ways to reach it — plus how it differs from the Mansa Devi temple in Haridwar.
q: Where is Mansa Devi temple in Panchkula and what are its timings?
answer: Mata Mansa Devi Temple stands in the Shivalik foothills at Bilaspur village, Panchkula district, Haryana — about 10 km from the Chandigarh bus terminus. Built in 1811–1815 by Raja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra, it is run by a Shrine Board. Darshan is 4 am–10 pm in summer and 5 am–9 pm in winter. It is not the hill temple in Haridwar.
facts: main temple built by Raja Gopal Singh
intro: Shri Mata Mansa Devi Mandir — श्री माता मनसा देवी मंदिर — is the best-loved Devi shrine of the Chandigarh tricity. Mansa Devi is worshipped as a form of Shakti, the goddess who knows the wishes (mansa) of the mind. In the sanctum she is worshipped not as a large idol but as three pindis — natural stones.

Not the Haridwar temple. There are two famous Mansa Devi temples. This one is in Panchkula, Haryana, on the Shivalik foothills, and vehicles reach the complex. The other is on Bilwa Parvat above Haridwar, Uttarakhand, reached by a ropeway. The traditional Nau Devi Yatra visits the Panchkula temple.

story.lead: A cow, three stones and a devoted raja — the hill's story as the Shrine Board and local tradition tell it.
beats: Long ago, it is said, a cow climbed this Shivalik hill every day and let its milk flow over three stones lying side by side.
Villagers began to worship the stones. In local tradition, kept by the Shrine Board, the three pindis are linked to the forehead of Sati.
Raja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra was so devoted that, legend says, he came to the goddess every day with his queen through a tunnel about 3 km long from his fort.
He built the present temple between 1811 and 1815. In 1840 Maharaja Karam Singh of Patiala added a Shiva temple close by, the Patiala Shivalaya.
more: After the princely states merged, royal patronage ended and the shrine was neglected for years. In 1991 Haryana passed the Shri Mata Mansa Devi Shrine Act, and a Shrine Board has run the complex since — about 100 acres of temples, courtyards and pilgrim facilities. Look for the fine 19th-century wall paintings in the temple complex.

dates.note: Lakhs of devotees come for each mela. The board usually arranges free e-rickshaws for elders and differently-abled devotees during Navratri — check its notices before you go.

reach.h2: How to reach Mansa Devi temple, Panchkula
cards: About 4 km from Panchkula bus stand and about 10 km from the Chandigarh bus terminus. Vehicles reach the temple complex; Delhi is about 272 km away.
Chandigarh railway station is about 13 km away; Kalka about 25 km.
Chandigarh airport is about 19 km by road.
Chandi Mandir is about 10 km away and Kali Mata Mandir, Kalka about 25 km; Naina Devi in Bilaspur is about 110 km.

items: One of the easiest Devi shrines to visit: close to the city, with vehicles reaching the complex. Avoid the Ashtami and Navami crowds of Navratri with elders.
Queues build from the morning aarti. Weekday mornings outside the melas are the calmest.
Dress modestly, remove footwear and follow the Shrine Board's instructions on photography.
For notices, donations or prasad, use the Shrine Board's own website, mansadevi.org.in — beware of look-alike sites.

itinerary.h2: A simple Mansa Devi trip from Chandigarh
days: Mansa Devi, Chandi Mandir and Pinjore
Early darshan at Mansa Devi and the Patiala Shivalaya; on to Chandi Mandir; afternoon at Kali Mata Mandir, Kalka and the Pinjore (Yadavindra) Gardens.
Drive to Naina Devi in Bilaspur (about 110 km) and continue on the Himachal Shakti Peeth circuit to Chintpurni and Jwala Ji.

faqs: What are Mansa Devi temple Panchkula timings?
In summer 4 am to 10 pm, in winter 5 am to 9 pm, as published by the Shrine Board. Bhog is offered from 11 to 11:15 am. The changeover dates are not published, so confirm locally.
What is the Mansa Devi aarti time?
Summer: 4:30–5 am and 7–7:30 pm. Winter: 5:30–6 am and 6–6:30 pm (Shrine Board).
Is Mansa Devi Panchkula a Shakti Peeth?
Local tradition and the Shrine Board link the three pindis to Sati's forehead, but the temple is not in the classical lists of 51 Shakti Peeths. It is revered as one of the Nau Devi goddesses.
Raja Gopal Singh of Mani Majra built the present temple between 1811 and 1815. The nearby Patiala Shivalaya was added in 1840 by Maharaja Karam Singh of Patiala.
How far is Mansa Devi from Chandigarh?
About 10 km from the Chandigarh bus terminus, about 13 km from Chandigarh railway station and about 19 km from the airport.
Is Mansa Devi Panchkula the same as Mansa Devi Haridwar?
No. The Panchkula temple is in Haryana's Shivalik foothills and vehicles reach it. The Haridwar temple is on Bilwa Parvat in Uttarakhand and is reached by a ropeway.
When is the Navratri mela at Mansa Devi?
Twice a year, for the nine days of Chaitra and Ashvin Navratri. The next mela begins with Chaitra Navratri on 7 April 2027.
Which Mansa Devi is in the Nau Devi Yatra?
The Panchkula temple. It is one of the nine Devis of the traditional yatra, usually visited early in the route.
